sentences.text: The genus name Gobititan combines the Gobi Desert region and Greek Titans to reflect the animal's large size, while the specific name shenzhouensis refers to Shenzhou, an ancient name for China.
Gobititan possessed a relatively high number of tail vertebrae compared to advanced titanosaurs, a trait interpreted as basal.
Gregory S. Paul estimated that Gobititan reached a length of 20 meters and a weight of 20 metric tons.
The animal is distinguished by the presence of a fifth digit on its foot, a trait unknown in other titanosaurs.
Fossils of Gobititan were discovered in the Gongpoquan Basin in Gansu, China, during the summer of 1999.
The type specimen is a partial skeleton containing 41 tail vertebrae and an incomplete left hindlimb, and the species Gobititan shenzhouensis was named and described by You, Tang, and Luo in 2003.
Gobititan was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur living during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
Recent research generally classifies Gobititan as a titanosauriform and a member of the Somphospondyli.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Gobititan as Euhelopodidae.
Gobititan lived during the Albian stage, between 113.2 and 110.1 million years ago.
Some scientific analyses still classify Gobititan as a titanosaur despite recent trends placing it in Somphospondyli.
